calls.headline: Dollar rises 35 piasters to EGP 53.86 despite foreign debt buying
calls.body: The central bank's rate closed Sunday at EGP 53.72 to buy and 53.86 to sell, against 53.50 on Thursday, a rise of 35 piasters on the day (central bank, Sada Elbalad, Al-Ain). It came although Arab and foreign investors bought a net $342.9m of government debt on the secondary market on Thursday and more than $2bn over the four sessions to Thursday (EGX data via Al-Ain); Al Mal put foreigners' net buying of bonds and bills at EGP 101.5bn for the week. Parliament's economic committee meets on Monday on a request to explain the dollar's rise (Masrawy). The EGX30 still rose 0.31% to 52,187.20, and foreigners were net buyers of EGP 77.9m of shares.
calls.view: A dollar at 19-month highs abroad and a US 10-year at 5.15% are pulling on every emerging currency, and the pound is giving back part of its gain rather than breaking: at EGP 53.86 it is still about 1.7% firmer than on November 5. As long as bill auctions draw bids well above the amount sold, the desk keeps the dollar inside EGP 52–55, at medium confidence. Banks gain from the carry either way; importers lose a little of the margin they won in October.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a bill auction clears with bids below the amount offered.

calls.headline: MOPCO's nine-month profit jumps 56% to EGP 12.1bn
calls.line: Fertilizer prices outran the gas cuts; the stock rose 3.7% on Sunday.
calls.body: MOPCO's net profit after tax rose to EGP 12.14bn in January–September from EGP 7.78bn, on sales up 47% to EGP 27.39bn; gross profit rose 50% to EGP 14.20bn (Egypt Oil & Gas, Power News). Its board also approved a $165m bank loan for plant upgrades. The stock rose 3.67% to EGP 40.70 on Sunday and Abu Qir 1.9% to EGP 78.96 (TradingView).
calls.view: Urea near $530–540 a ton is paying for the gas cuts, so the desk's view that rationing keeps fertilizer stocks under pressure is being tested by profits, not by supply. The desk keeps it, at low confidence now: Abu Qir sits about EGP 6 under the EGP 85 line, and any end to the cuts would end the call.
calls.wrong: Abu Qir closes above EGP 85 before November 30, or the government restores full gas supply to the plants.
calls.notice: Al-Manassa reported, from two unnamed sources, that the government raised the gas price for fertilizer plants by 50% in exchange for exempting them from the subsidized local quota; no second outlet has confirmed it, and the view does not rely on it.

calls.headline: Palm Hills' profit slips 4.7% as margins shrink
calls.line: Revenue rose 24% but the gross margin fell to 35% from 41%.
calls.body: Palm Hills' nine-month consolidated profit attributable to shareholders fell to EGP 3.37bn from EGP 3.54bn, Youm7 reported from its filing, while revenue rose 24.4% to EGP 31.80bn; the gross margin fell to 35.1% from 40.8%. Profit before minorities was EGP 3.68bn against EGP 3.70bn (Alboslanews). Talaat Moustafa's attributable profit rose 11.9% to EGP 11.72bn, slower than its 24% revenue growth (Arab Finance).
calls.view: Both big developers are selling more and keeping less: costs and financing at 25% bill yields eat the gain from higher prices. That supports the desk's view that developers lag the EGX30 while rates stay high, judged November 27, at low confidence because a rate cut in December or Ras El-Hekma's land sales could turn it.
calls.wrong: Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills together beat the EGX30 between October 30 and November 27.

calls.headline: Edita's third-quarter profit rises 41.5% on record sales
calls.line: Revenue rose 32.9% to EGP 7.3bn; the stock opened Monday about 5% higher.
calls.body: Edita's third-quarter net profit rose 41.5% to EGP 938.1m on record revenue of EGP 7.3bn, up 32.9%; the gross margin fell to 32.9% from 35% (Arab Finance, EnterpriseAM). The company put nine-month profit at EGP 2.4bn, up 54%, and exports at EGP 1.84bn, up 40%. The stock traded about 5% above Sunday's EGP 19.23 in Monday's first hour (TradingView).
calls.view: Volume and price both grew while the margin held near 33%, the kind of quarter that keeps food producers among the desk's preferred sectors after Juhayna's 33% profit rise. Medium confidence: a weaker pound helps exports but raises imported costs.
calls.wrong: Edita closes back below EGP 18.50, under Sunday's level, before December 15.

calls.headline: Chip rout spreads to Asia a day before Nvidia's results
calls.body: Taiwan's Taiex fell more than 4% on Monday and Nasdaq 100 futures 0.5%, after the cash index lost 1.2% on Friday, when AMD fell 8.8% and Broadcom 4.8% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, Investing.com). Nvidia, at $162.85, has shed about $1.9tn of market value since early October as investors question the debt-funded AI buildout (LSEG via Reuters). It reports on Tuesday after the close, its first quarter since Jensen Huang left as chief executive: guidance was $108bn of revenue, against $57.0bn a year earlier (10-Q).
calls.view: Tuesday is the week's only real test: at about 12 times expected earnings Nvidia is priced for disappointment, so guidance at or above $108bn and a clear word on the chief executive could set off a sharp rebound in the chip names. The desk does not call the direction; it expects the selling to pause into the report and the move afterward to set the sector's tone into December. Medium confidence that the Nasdaq holds above 24,000 into November 20.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes below 24,000 before November 20.

calls.headline: December hike odds hold near 89% after softer producer prices
calls.line: A 0.3% rise in October prices did not change the Fed's path; the 10-year is at 5.15%.
calls.body: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October against 0.4% expected, and 6.5% from a year earlier, the most since November 2022 (BLS via InvestmentNews, AFP via Yahoo). CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point hike on December 9 at 88.5% and a half point at 11.5% on Saturday, with the federal funds range at 3.75–4% (Cryptonews, BigGo). The 2-year yield closed Friday at 4.88% and the 10-year at 5.15% (Treasury). Wednesday's minutes show how many officials wanted to move in October.
calls.view: A hike in December is priced; the question is whether it is one and done. A 5.15% 10-year makes the S&P 500 at about 7,560 dear against bonds, but earnings are still rising, so the desk keeps its view that the index holds above 7,250 into December 9, at medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes below 7,250 before December 9.

calls.headline: Bitcoin hits $62,006, its lowest since July
calls.line: Down about 15% in 11 days as US Bitcoin funds see outflows.
calls.body: Bitcoin fell to $62,006 on Sunday on Binance, its lowest since July (Yahoo Finance, CoinMarketCap), and traded near $64,355 on Monday morning (CoinGecko), about 29% below its September high of $87,364. US spot Bitcoin funds had seven straight days of outflows, $1.91bn in all (Yahoo Finance).
calls.view: Bitcoin is trading as the riskiest end of the same trade that is hurting chip stocks: dearer money and a stronger dollar. The desk expects no turn before the Fed's December 9 decision, at low confidence, since crypto can reverse on a single good day for Nvidia.

calls.headline: Brent slips to $95.30 on surplus forecasts
calls.line: The IEA expects a surplus this quarter; the desk's $105 line holds.
calls.body: Brent fell 54 cents to $95.30 early on Monday and WTI 0.3% to $88.34, after the IEA said on Friday that the world market returns to surplus in the fourth quarter and China's October refinery runs fell (Reuters via Shafaq). IMF PortWatch still counts about four ships a day through Hormuz, against 85 a year earlier.
calls.view: With a surplus forecast and Gulf supply finding other routes, the desk keeps its view that Brent stays below $105 into November 20, raising its confidence to medium with four sessions to go. Cheaper oil helps Egypt's import bill and the pound.

drivers.name: Foreign money in bills
drivers.why: Arab and foreign investors bought a net $342.9m of government debt on the secondary market on Thursday and more than $2bn over the four sessions to Thursday (EGX data via Al-Ain); Al Mal put foreigners' net buying of bonds and bills at EGP 101.5bn for the week.

drivers.why: $13bn in July–September, up 20.4%, and $38.2bn in nine months, the economy's largest single source of dollars (central bank via EnterpriseAM).

drivers.name: A stronger dollar abroad
drivers.why: The US 10-year yield closed at 5.15% on Friday and futures give about 88.5% odds of a December Fed hike (CME FedWatch); the dollar's strength took the pound 35 piasters weaker on Sunday.

drivers.name: State land for debt
drivers.why: A decree lets the Finance Ministry use 26,690 feddans in the Red Sea governorate to cut public debt as well as back sukuk; budget-sector debt was 83.9% of GDP in March (Daily News Egypt).

drivers.name: Suez traffic recovers
drivers.why: IMF PortWatch counts 43.7 Suez transits a day over October 26–November 8, against 41.6 a year earlier, while Bab el-Mandeb traffic is still about a quarter lower; October's revenue was $724m.

drivers.name: Lost export dollars from gas cuts
drivers.why: Fertilizer plants lose 33% of their gas with no end date, and Brent's jump to $95.82 raises the fuel import bill.

view.headline: Bills and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The pound fell 35 piasters on Sunday while foreigners kept buying bills, which says the move came from the dollar's strength abroad rather than money leaving. Foreign bill buying and record remittances still outweigh a firmer dollar, so the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55 into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risks are a half-point Fed hike, dearer oil and export dollars lost to gas cuts.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a bill auction clears with bids below the amount offered.
